title: Report's job is surfacing reasoning, not collecting material
framing: Started from the assumption that the hard part of status reports is material collection — remembering by Friday what happened on Monday.

alternatives.option: Team-leader aggregation mode (merge reports from reports)
alternatives.rejected_because: different problem: dedup and status rollup, not reasoning capture

alternatives.option: Both personal and aggregation modes behind one skill
alternatives.rejected_because: materially higher complexity for a second use case that isn't needed yet

decision: Scope to individual upward reporting, with the explicit requirement that the report surface the author's own thinking, mined from their AI conversations.
outcome: Reframed the whole design: the skill is a decision capturer whose output format happens to be a report.

evidence.quote: 向上汇报。我希望日报周报中能体现我的思考。这个思考是从我和ai的对话中总结出来的。

title: Conversation transcripts as a first-class source, calendar and chat dropped
framing: Assumed git plus an optional calendar connector would cover the material.

alternatives.rejected_because: needs a connector that isn't reliably available
highest integration cost of the four; likely degenerates into manual paste

constraint: Only sources readable without external credentials were viable.
decision: Git/PR + manual notes + Claude Code transcripts, with the user's own messages and their endorsements of assistant replies as the thinking signal.
outcome: Verified transcripts are parseable: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl, human turns isolated by origin.kind == 'human' and absence of toolUseResult; AskUserQuestion stores both the chosen answer and the options passed over.
open_question: Whether claude.ai (non-CLI) conversations can be reached at all; currently out of scope.

transcript parser, verified against the live session

title: Daily run is an ingest; weekly consumes a journal, not transcripts
framing: Conventional split treats daily and weekly as the same report at two granularities.

alternatives.rejected_because: dailies are event-shaped; concatenating them cannot produce outcomes, and the rejected-alternative detail is already gone by then

alternatives.option: Weekly re-parses a week of raw transcripts
alternatives.rejected_because: a week of transcripts does not fit in context, and older sessions may have rolled

constraint: Transcripts are large and perishable; context is bounded.
decision: Daily mines transcripts into a durable structured journal (journal/YYYY-MM.jsonl) and the daily report is a byproduct. Weekly reads only the journal plus a full-week git pass.
outcome: Encoded in SKILL.md as two separate workflows with an explicit dependency: weekly accuracy requires daily to have run.
open_question: No enforcement that daily actually runs — a cron or SessionStart hook is the obvious next step but isn't built.

evidence.quote: Proposed in-session; user proceeded without objection rather than endorsing explicitly. Weak signal — recorded as such.

title: Collectors optimize for recall, model supplies precision

alternatives.option: Tight classifiers that only flag unambiguous approval/rejection
alternatives.rejected_because: a missed pushback is unrecoverable once the transcript ages out; a false positive costs the model one line of reading

constraint: Regex cannot distinguish 'ok, continue' from 'ok, that's the right design'; only a reader with context can.
decision: Endorsement/pushback patterns deliberately over-trigger; SKILL.md instructs the model to discard false positives and forbids tightening them.
outcome: Asymmetry documented in the script docstring so a future maintainer doesn't 'fix' it.
open_question: Patterns are hand-written for zh/en only.

evidence.quote: Design note: this script optimizes for RECALL, not precision.

title: Two silent data-loss bugs in the git collector
framing: Treated the git collector as the trivial half of the pipeline — a log wrapper, unlikely to be where correctness problems live.

alternatives.option: Ship the collector on the strength of it running without error
alternatives.rejected_because: both defects returned a clean empty/zero result rather than failing, so 'it ran' proved nothing

constraint: Both failures are invisible in normal use: one drops commits, the other zeroes magnitude, and neither raises.
decision: Pass explicit T00:00:00 times to git rather than bare dates, and lead the pretty-format with the record separator instead of trailing it.
outcome: Same window went from 0 commits / 0 files to 1 commit / 11 files / +1132. Both root causes are now commented at the site so they are not re-introduced.

evidence.quote: git log --since=2026-09-15 excluded a commit made at 00:24:32 while the clock read 00:24:48 — approxidate fills a missing time-of-day with the current time, not midnight, so a daily run silently drops everything committed earlier that day.
--numstat prints the stat block AFTER the formatted header, so a trailing record separator slices each commit's numstat onto the front of the next record.
explicit time bounds + leading record separator

title: Verified the transcript source's guarantees before relying on them
framing: Had treated 'CLI conversations are recorded locally, verbatim' as settled after parsing one live session successfully. Parsing a file proves the format, not the guarantee.

alternatives.option: Keep the assumption on the strength of the parser working
alternatives.rejected_because: a working parser says nothing about retention, scope, or which sessions land on disk at all

constraint: The whole design rests on this source; a wrong assumption here invalidates the weekly report silently rather than loudly.
decision: Checked the docs and the local filesystem. Transcripts are complete and plaintext, but bounded by four limits, all now documented in SKILL.md and README: 30-day default cleanupPeriodDays retention; local CLI sessions only (web/remote run in ephemeral VMs); .orphaned- copies double-count; nothing is encrypted and credentials printed by tools land in the transcript.
outcome: Retention ceiling is 30 days, which converts 'daily should run' into 'daily must run'. Also found and fixed a real defect the assumption had hidden: the collector's */*.jsonl glob matched set-aside .orphaned- transcripts, doubling every prompt from an affected session.
open_question: No way to mine Claude Code on the web sessions at all; if much of the work happens there, coverage is worse than it looks.

evidence.quote: 你确定所有的cli的聊天对话原文都记录在本地了是吧。

Docs, data-usage: 'Claude Code clients store session transcripts locally in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/ for 30 days by default to enable session resumption. Adjust the period with cleanupPeriodDays.'
